metadata.title: Qualcomm upgrade, Intel initiation among today's top calls on Wall Street

content.text:
The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.
Top 5 Upgrades:
-
Morgan Stanley upgraded Qualcomm (QCOM) to Equal Weight from Underweight with a price target of $231, up from $146. The firm, which says "we have been wrong to be skeptical," states after the company's investor day that $5B of guidance for AI data center sales in FY27 from a proven management team "clearly pushes them into the AI beneficiaries category."
-
Erste Group upgraded Micron (MU) to Buy from Hold. Micron announced "very high revenue guidance" for the next quarter due to strong memory demand, with the gross margin rising to 86%, notes the analyst.
-
Barclays upgraded Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) to Overweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $36, up from $30. The company's improved leverage and "waning" transaction uncertainty brings opportunity for a share re-rating as the planned coffee business separation draws closer, the analyst says.
-
Goldman Sachs upgraded Primoris (PRIM) to Neutral from Sell with a price target of $102, down from $107. The stock has fallen 25% since the firm initiated shares at sell in November of 2025 as Goldman Sachs highlighted its exposure to long-cycle growth themes but believed 2026 Solar estimates were too high, the analyst tells investors in a research note.
-
Monness Crespi upgraded Workday (WDAY) to Buy from Neutral with a $150 price target. Shares are down 45% in 2026 and down 62% from peak reached in early 2024, notes the analyst, who views the depressed valuation as "enticing."
Top 5 Downgrades:
-
Morgan Stanley downgraded Affirm (AFRM) to Equal Weight from Overweight with an unchanged price target of $79. The market now appreciates the "durability" of the company's growth, funding, and credit, the analyst tells investors in a research note.
-
BofA downgraded PVH Corp. (PVH) to Underperform from Neutral with a price target of $70, down from $90. As a result of conflict in the Middle East, PVH is experiencing softer demand in Europe alongside sales and margin headwinds in its Middle East and Turkiye businesses, says the analyst.
-
Truist downgraded Exelixis (EXEL) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $54, up from $51, after assuming coverage of the name. The company's recent non-liver metastases topline miss for zanzalintinib "introduces risk," the analyst tells investors in a research note.
-
Barclays downgraded Brown-Forman (BF.B) to Equal Weight from Overweight with an unchanged price target of $27. The firm cites valuation for the downgrade, saying Brown-Forman's risk/reward proposition is appropriately captured at current share levels.
-
Lake Street downgraded Identiv (INVE) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $4, down from $6, after the company announced it was selling its IoT assets, including its German R&D center and Thai manufacturing operation, to Trackonomy. With the launch of Identiv's new strategy, the firm is "pleased to see something finally announced," but it believes "most investors will be underwhelmed." Craig-Hallum also downgraded Identiv to Hold from Buy with a $3.10 price target.
